sections.title: The Scope of the Meeting Notes
sections.content:
RFC 164 is a set of notes from a Network Working Group meeting identified in its title as taking place from May 16 through May 19, 1971. The preface says the notes are for reference and recall by attendees and that the author did not try to make them complete or understandable to people who were not there.

The notes are arranged chronologically. The preface warns that some schedules and tasks differ within the document because plans changed; later dates are meant to take precedence over earlier ones.
sections.plainLanguage: These are working notes, not a full explanation of everything discussed. The author says readers should treat later schedule details as updates to earlier plans.

sections.title: Site Reports and Network Work
sections.content:
The notes include reports from ARPA network sites about their computers, host software, and services. Reports describe work on NCP, logger and Telnet services, file transfer, terminal interfaces, and data services. Some entries describe systems already in operation; others record plans or expected schedules as reported at the meeting.

The notes also discuss the Network Information Center's planned services and documentation, Telnet design questions, file-transfer work, socket naming, the Initial Connection Protocol, testing and validation, operating systems, data management, terminal IMPs, and the organization of the Network Working Group.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites reported what software and services they had running or planned. Participants also discussed how to connect, transfer files, manage data, test implementations, and organize future work.

sections.title: Issues Raised and Follow-Up Work
sections.content:
Several discussions resulted in committees or plans for further work. The notes mention efforts to refine the Initial Connection Protocol, develop file and data-management protocols, and address socket structures. Participants discussed splitting file transfer into a data-transfer component and a file mechanism, with an RFC expected to describe the work.

The final sessions list committees and anticipated publication or implementation dates, followed by additional comments about network support and organization. These are meeting records and forecasts; the RFC does not present them as a complete later outcome report.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting identified tasks for groups to continue after the sessions. The dates in the notes are plans recorded at that time, not confirmation that the work was later completed.
